observations: RIME Figure 8 is explicitly identified as the verso of the single joined Cat.1883 plus Cat.2095 five-fragment support; the TIFF is 6595 by 4710 pixels.
The volume 1 printed page 41 item 2 is an edition text entry; Plate XXIX's right-hand nine-row panel is the recto text panel, while a separate upper-left panel depicts the reverse.

The historical reverse panel is sparse and numbered one through seven. Figure 8 shows a photographed verso with a different, fuller visible layout; a shared support and a broadly similar line orientation do not identify a particular line across the drawing and photograph.

The previous image box [2800,1690,6500,2020] is expressed in original TIFF pixels, but there is no valid geometric transform from the p. 41 item 2 recto text locus to this verso box. No line box or sign sequence was copied from modern RIME editorial text.

coordinate_comparison.reason: The source locator is a recto text locus and the pinned photograph is the verso; a numeric transform would imply false physical line identity.

rationale: The W10 p. 41 item 2 locator resolves to the recto text panel of Plate XXIX, but the pinned RIME Figure 8 is the verso; the proposed source-exact pair therefore fails side identity.

Plate XXIX also includes a separate reverse panel, but its sparse drawing cannot be assigned to a diagnostic line of the photograph from support identity, orientation, and line count alone. That second comparison remains unresolved.
No independent palaeographic reviewer was available. The result is a negative candidate decision, not DATA-004 gold, training admission, benchmark clearance, or a reviewed line pair.
